body: Sankaran Naren, CIO (equity) of ICICI Prudential AMC, India's best-known institutional contrarian. Process: buy what has underperformed and is out of favour; shift between equity, debt and gold based on valuation (the house Balanced Advantage approach raises equity when valuations are low and cuts it when high - characterisation of the model); stress-test with history (the 1994-2004 'lost decade' in Indian mid/small caps). Documented calls: Feb 2025 (IFA Galaxy) - said median P/E of mid/small caps at ~43x was 'absurd' and unsustainable, more expensive than 2008, and questioned SIPs/fresh money in those categories; by then the Smallcap 250 had already fallen ~24% from its Sept 2024 peak, and it lagged through 2025. Aug 2025 - warned of 1990s-like risk. Feb 2026 - 'mega gains are unlikely now', large caps not meaningfully overvalued, small/mid caps significantly overvalued. Mistake/limitation: his caution on small caps started in 2023, and small caps rallied hard through Sept 2024 before falling - valuation-based calls are directionally useful but early (characterisation). Copyable: a rule-based allocation that lowers equity (especially small caps) as median P/E and IPO froth rise, and adds after 1-2 years of underperformance; pair with lump-sum deployment into large caps when they are unloved.
